subtitle: Taking a position in writing, and je … desto
words.intro: In Lusatia a huge open-cast mine has eaten whole villages. Elsewhere, next to wind farms, people are writing long letters about the view. Energy is the one subject on which every German has a position, in writing.

grammar[0].blocks[2].title: The classic mistake
grammar[0].blocks[2].text: Not *Meiner Meinung nach, dass …* but *Meiner Meinung nach überwiegen die Vorteile.*
grammar[0].blocks[3].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[0].fact: A *Leserbrief* to a German paper may be printed under your real name and street, which rather raises the stakes. Local papers still treat them seriously, and in small towns the letters page is read before the news.

grammar[1].subheading: je … desto, and the verbs of a discussion
grammar[1].blocks[0].title: Two clauses, two places
grammar[1].blocks[0].note: After *je* the verb goes last. After *desto* comes the comparative, and then the verb right away.
grammar[1].blocks[0].rows[0].en: The sooner we act, the better it is.
grammar[1].blocks[0].rows[1].en: The more it rains, the higher the river rises.
grammar[1].blocks[0].rows[2].en: The older I get, the less I know.
grammar[1].blocks[1].title: Verbs for a discussion
grammar[1].blocks[1].note: zustimmen and widersprechen take the dative: *Ihnen*, not *Sie*.
grammar[1].fact: Every German neighbourhood now has someone with solar panels on the roof, and a chart of it on their phone. They’ll show you, whether you asked or not. Sunny days are discussed like football results.

document.intro: A real placard in a meadow in Marienmünster, against a new power line. Green electricity has to reach the south from the wind farms in the north, and every field in between has a view on the matter. Note the words: *Monster*, *Lebensgefahr*.
document.fact: Germany needs thousands of kilometres of new power lines to carry wind power south, and local protest has held them up for years, forcing many underground, at much greater cost. *Unter Strom* can also mean in a state of great excitement, so this sign has made a little joke.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Write what you think of this placard.
document.tasks[1].note: Your own view: check the verb right after nach, last after ob.
reading.intro: A wind turbine is planned on the hill above a village. A letter arrives at the local paper, and it is a model of German form: claim, argument, counter-argument, conclusion. Vroni reads it aloud at the newsroom coffee machine. Only the last paragraph is a surprise.
reading.fact: Germany has torn down whole villages for brown coal, Lützerath as recently as 2023. *NIMBY* has its own German form: *Sankt-Florians-Prinzip*, after a saint invoked in an old prayer: spare my house, set fire to someone else’s. It applies to bypasses, wind turbines and refugee housing alike.
